sections.heading: Should a 20-Year-Old Roof Be Replaced? Repair vs. Replacement for East Orange Homes

runs.v: Not automatically, and East Orange homeowners should not accept a replacement pitch on age alone. A 3-tab asphalt roof reaches the end of its typical 20-year life around then, while an architectural roof is rated about 30 years, per InterNACHI, so age starts the conversation and an inspection of the existing conditions finishes it. Roof replacements are usually triggered by signs like widespread leaks, granule loss across the field, soft decking, or significant damage to the structure; a few missing shingles or one failed pipe boot calls for a roof repair in East Orange instead, since minor repairs typically cost $300 to $700.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Roofers use a rule of thumb that once damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, a full replacement costs less in the long run than continued repairs, and New Jersey's code sets a matching line for permits: on commercial, multi-family, and attached buildings, work on more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. For long-term value, treat a new roof as an investment in the whole building, since every layer, flashing, and vent is renewed at once.

faqs.q: Does East Orange require a permit for roof replacement?

runs.v: A full tear-off and replacement of the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and requires no construction permit, inspection, or notice to the construction official, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. A commercial, multi-family, or attached building crosses the 25% rule and requires a permit through the East Orange Building Division, a designated State Uniform Construction Code enforcement agency at 44 City Hall Plaza. A structural change to rafters, trusses, or ridge beams triggers a permit on any building.

faqs.q: Should I replace or repair my East Orange apartment-building roof?

runs.v: Replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost; repair when the damage stays localized on an asphalt roof under 10–15 years old. The 25–30% area rule and the 50% cost rule are contractor-consensus thresholds, and a localized repair can cost 5 to 10 times less than replacement, per Home Depot cost data. On a low-slope apartment roof, ponding water held more than 48 hours counts as a defect and signals a system at the end of service, per NRCA and ARMA.

faqs.q: Can I phase a roof replacement across the buildings in my East Orange apartment portfolio?

runs.v: Phased replacement spreads capital across budget cycles by prioritizing the buildings showing active leaks or structural concerns first, then working through the remaining stock. Standardizing on a single membrane system across the portfolio simplifies future maintenance, and a Newark Quality Roofing written estimate sets the scope and condition priority for each building before any tear-off begins.

faqs.q: Does a roof replacement on a Register-listed East Orange building need historic approval?

runs.v: East Orange has no identified local historic-preservation ordinance, so a Certificate of Appropriateness is not triggered, and National Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded replacement, per the National Park Service. Check current local requirements with the City of East Orange before the tear-off is scheduled.

faqs.q: Which roofing material suits a roof replacement in East Orange?

runs.v: Roof-replacement material matches the building and budget across asphalt at a 20-to-30-year life, metal at 40 to 80 years, slate at 60 to 150 years, and low-slope membrane at 7 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart. East Orange's pre-war walk-ups and apartment buildings carry flat and near-flat roofs suited to EPDM, TPO, or modified bitumen, while pitched single-family homes in the northern neighborhoods take architectural asphalt, metal, or slate. A new asphalt roof recoups roughly 60 to 68% of project cost at resale, per the Zonda Cost vs Value report.
